clue.text: Not a rise negotiated for a foreign girl

indicators.note: negotiated suggests the letters of the phrase are worked round into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A worker turned down for a pay increase after bargaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiated' rearranges NOTARISE, the letters of 'Not a rise', into the Spanish word for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A señorita is a young unmarried Spanish woman, so a girl from abroad.

clue.text: Seeds gaining entree?

definitions.meaning: small oil seeds used on bread
the password in Ali Baba that opened the cave

explanation.surface: Seeds that let you in somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open sesame' is the magic password in the Ali Baba tale.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a plant seed, and the magic word that opens the robbers' cave.

clue.text: Standard of Roman revolutionary figure

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning the letters over into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a figure

explanation.surface: The flag of an ancient Roman rebel leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges ROMAN to NORMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal and standard both mean usual or typical.

clue.text: Books to do with benefits available

parts.note: re means concerning
serves means benefits, is of use

explanation.surface: Library volumes concerning welfare payments on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books' is a verb here, as in booking a table.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a seat is to reserve it.

clue.text: A joiner making a row

definitions.meaning: a level or rank, as of seats

explanation.surface: A carpenter building a line of seating.
explanation.definitionFit: One who ties joins things; a tier is a rank of seats.

clue.text: Empty one container into another

indicators.note: into here asks for one piece to be put inside the other

parts.note: a vat is another sort of container
a can is one kind of container

explanation.surface: Instructions to pour the contents of one vessel into a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one container' and 'another' read as a set of nesting vessels; the definition 'Empty' sits at the front disguised as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacant and empty are synonyms describing something with nothing inside.

clue.text: Unwilling to declare a point

parts.note: to aver is to declare
SE, south-east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Reluctant to state an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse means being opposed or reluctant.

clue.text: Scholar embraced by a teetotal woman in court

indicators.note: embraced by means one piece is held inside another

parts.note: her is a woman
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: An academic hugged by a non-drinking lady in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced by' puts the graduate inside the woman. A barrister who has been called to the bar practises in court.
explanation.definitionFit: The bar is the court's dock or advocates' rail.

clue.text: Allow the French following to dress down

indicators.note: following places the French article after the word to

parts.note: le is French for the
to rate is to scold

explanation.surface: Permitting the French to wear casual clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress down' looks like casual wear but means scold, an old sense of RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate is to permit or put up with.

clue.text: Rejected sweets, but still put weight on

indicators.note: rejected as in turned back, so the word for sweets is read backwards

parts.note: sweets are desserts, the pudding course

explanation.surface: A dieter turns down puddings yet still gains pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns DESSERTS round. 'put weight on' looks like gaining weight but means emphasised.
explanation.definitionFit: To put weight on a point is to emphasise it.

clue.text: Split nearly all the income from property

parts.note: a split is a rent, a tear

indicators.note: nearly says the following word loses its final letter

parts.note: the word all, written out

explanation.surface: Landlords dividing up nearly every penny they collect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts the last L off ALL, leaving AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Rental is the money a landlord receives for letting out a building.

clue.text: Fine plan, yet to be licked into shape

indicators.note: licked into shape means the letters are knocked into a new form

explanation.surface: A good scheme still needing work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be licked into shape' rearranges PLANYET.
explanation.definitionFit: A penalty is a fine or punishment.

clue.text: Many a bore is just inadequate

parts.note: M is a Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
an eagre is a tidal bore, a wave surging up a river

explanation.surface: A tedious person is simply not good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a dull person, but it is the tidal wave called an EAGRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or insufficient in amount.

clue.text: Such clothing makes some people use strong language!

parts.note: men are some people
to swear is to use strong language

explanation.surface: Some garments are so awful they make people curse.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing designed for males is sold as menswear in shops.

clue.text: Let out — repeatedly let out

parts.note: re means again
to lease is to rent out

explanation.surface: Releasing something then renting it again.
explanation.definitionFit: To release is to free or set loose.

clue.text: An old soldier — never at assembly

indicators.note: assembly suggests the letters are put together again in a new order

explanation.surface: A retired serviceman who never attends a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' rearranges NEVERAT, the letters of 'never at'.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone who has served long in the armed forces.

clue.text: Keep going, though behind everybody else

explanation.surface: A runner who keeps on despite trailing the field.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense means endure; the adjective sense means final in a sequence.

clue.text: Tea with nothing added? Divine!

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
plain means unadorned

explanation.surface: Praise for unadulterated tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective but is a noun: a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A divine is a cleric, as a chaplain is.

clue.text: Give voice about legal wrong in Norwegian parliament

indicators.note: about means one word wraps round another

parts.note: to sing is to give voice
a tort is a civil wrong

explanation.surface: Speaking out about an injustice in Oslo's legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the singing round the civil wrong; the Storting is Norway's parliament in Oslo.
explanation.definitionFit: The Storting is the Norwegian legislature.

clue.text: Music composed without a note being written

definitions.text: Music composed without a note being written

parts.words: Music composed without a note being written
parts.note: evening music sung under a window; the phrase plays on improvising for a loved one

explanation.surface: Music created without a score.
explanation.definitionFit: A song sung beneath a lover's window.

clue.text: Capital investment in a firm that seems reliable

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Financial jargon about putting money into a sound company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks financial but is the head (Latin caput), so its investment is headgear; 'in' finds the answer inside the words 'that seems'.
explanation.definitionFit: Headgear is what one puts on one's capital, that is, the head.

clue.text: Clear of all charges, went ahead, and so caused a certain irritation

parts.note: nett means with all deductions taken off
led means went in front

explanation.surface: A businessman irritated after his costs were deducted.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'certain irritation' is a sting, as from the stinging plant.
explanation.definitionFit: To be nettled is to be annoyed, as if stung by the plant.

clue.text: Port is drunk for good health

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: Drinking port for health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges PORTIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a German toast meaning may it benefit.

clue.text: Twins for example brought up on very little

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means read upwards

parts.note: eg is for example
mini means very small

explanation.surface: Twins given an example to look up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' in a down clue reads the abbreviation upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini is the sign of the twins in the zodiac.

clue.text: The attitude taken by a high-minded individual over an engineer

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above the rest

parts.note: ST is saint
CE is civil engineer

explanation.surface: A saintly person condescending to an engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is an attitude or position.

clue.text: An Irish resort that's left with considerable speed!

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a rush is great haste

explanation.surface: Someone dashing away from a seaside town in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: PORTRUSH is a seaside town in County Antrim, Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is a well-known holiday spot on the Antrim coast.

clue.text: Depression about the City appears appropriate

indicators.note: about means one word goes round the other

parts.note: a dent is a hollow, a depression
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: An economic slump around London's financial district seems fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the dent round the City; EC is the City of London's postcode. 'Depression' and 'the City' suggest economics.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent means suitable or proper in the circumstances.

clue.text: Married before. Must be simple!

parts.note: m is married
ere means before

explanation.surface: Was married before — it must be easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means simple or nothing more than.

clue.text: Among a large number in the film

indicators.note: in here asks for one piece to be placed inside another

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on glass
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Being one of a crowd of extras in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts D inside MIST. 'film' looks like a movie but is a haze.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidst is a literary synonym for in the middle of.

clue.text: For a member of the family it's telling

definitions.meaning: the act of narrating a story

explanation.surface: Someone recounting stories about their kin.
explanation.definitionFit: Kin are relatives; a narration of events is also called this.

clue.text: Things look back whenever the outlook is black

indicators.note: look back is read as the letters being turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Matters seem gloomy whenever prospects are dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look back' rearranges the letters of 'Things'. 'black' outlook is literal darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: After dark the view outside is black, as in the hours of darkness.

clue.text: She'll have to be understanding about the heartless rogue

indicators.note: about tells us one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to be nice is to be kind and understanding

indicators.note: heartless means the inner letters are removed, keeping the outside ones

explanation.surface: A woman must be forgiving towards a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' keeps only the outer letters of 'rogue'; 'about' puts the kindly phrase round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Berenice is a female name, borne by several ancient queens.
